title: Action information is integrated into entorhinal representations of conceptual space and is reflected in eye movements
experiments_summary: The study involved 60 right-handed, healthy German-speaking participants tested over two consecutive days. Participants were trained to learn a repeating state-action graph in which numbers (states) were associated with specific numerical operations (actions: +1, -1, +2, -2), structured in repeating 5-number modules. Number-to-state mappings were shifted across participants to counterbalance pre-existing numerical associations. Day 1 (~2 hours) consisted of interleaved free-exploration and test training blocks (~40 blocks), followed by a recall task (4 runs, ~80 trials/run) during eyetracking with an EyeLink 1000 Plus at 1000 Hz. Day 2 (~1.5 hours) consisted of refresher training (~10 blocks), followed by a recall task (8 runs, ~80 trials/run) during fMRI. During the recall task, individual numbers were pseudorandomly presented and intermittent probe trials (16 per run) tested knowledge of afforded successors. Performance was measured via accuracy on test and probe trials, with reaction time differences across states analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA and post-hoc paired t-tests. Questionnaire data were collected to assess strategy use. For the eyetracking analysis, binocular gaze data were preprocessed (blink removal, smoothing), segmented per trial, and the relative horizontal gaze shift between states affording only positive versus only negative actions (states 2 vs. 3) was tested across time using temporal cluster correction (1-sample t-test, 10,000 permutations). Gaze lateralization was correlated with task performance using Pearson r. fMRI data were acquired on a 3T Siemens Prisma scanner (TR=1000ms, TE=22ms, 2.5mm isotropic voxels, multi-band factor 5, 65 slices) with fieldmap correction, and preprocessed using fMRIPrep 22.0.1 (including motion correction, slice-timing correction, fieldmap-based distortion correction, ICA-AROMA denoising, and 5mm FWHM smoothing). A first-level GLM extracted per-condition, per-run beta estimates in native subject space, modeling state identity as stick functions alongside motion, visual, and motor regressors. Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) was performed using cross-validated Mahalanobis (crossnobis) distances within anatomical ROIs (entorhinal cortex, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, visual cortex, motor cortex) derived from the Jülich Atlas and registered to subject space. Neural dissimilarity matrices were compared to model RDMs—an affordance model (shared actions between states), a link-distance model, and an affordance-magnitude model—using tie-corrected Spearman rank correlation, with partial correlations used to control for alternative models, reaction time confounds, and gaze-based retinotopic effects. Group-level inference used one-sample t-tests on Fisher z-scored correlations. A whole-brain searchlight RSA (3-voxel radius spheres, TFCE cluster correction) was also performed. Gaze position during fMRI was estimated using DeepMReye (a pre-trained CNN applied to eyeball MR signal at 10 Hz sub-TR resolution), and the resulting lateralization was compared across conditions via paired t-test and correlated with entorhinal neural distances and affordance model fit using Pearson r.
